UN Institute for Training and Research

description.narrative: Programme support to the UN Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR). Sida foresees a programme support that will allocate broadly on its programme content (through UNITAR’s strategic framework fund). The programme content is based on the five strategic objectives: Peace, People, Planet, Prosperity and Cross-fertilizing Knowledge and Expertise.

Programstöd till FN:s institut för kapacitetsutveckling. Sida planerar ett programstöd (genom UNITAR:s strategiska fond) som kommer att innefatta programmets fem strategiska delar: Fred, Människor, Planeten, Välstånd och Tvärsektoriellt lärande/Agenda 2030-kunskap.

UNITAR's mission is to develop the institutional and organisational capacities of countries and other United Nations stakeholders through high-quality learning solutions and related knowledge products and services to enhance decision-making and to support country-level action for overcoming global challenges. Sida foresees a four-year programme support to UNITAR to develop and scale-up its core activities in capacity development for the 2030 Agenda in the areas of peace, people, planet, prosperity and cross-fertilizing knowledge and expertise.

For instance, with Sida (and other cofunding) funding, the project Strengthening Knowledge and Skills to Address Climate Change and Advance Sustainable Development was implemented, with the objective to support the promotion of climate change learning and the implementation of National Climate Change Learning Strategies in UN CC:Learn partner countries.
In Kenya, UNITARs Division for Planet, as the Secretariat of the One UN Climate Change Learning Partnership (UN CC:Learn), UNITARs Division for Multilateral Diplomacy, the Foreign Service Academy, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Climate Change Directorate, Ministry of Environment and Forestry of Kenya joined forces to develop and deliver a Climate Diplomacy Online Training Programme.
The programme provided 36 Kenyan diplomats, government officials and civil society representatives with training on climate change and climate change diplomacy, the history of negotiations to date and the structure and functioning of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). It also built practical and in-depth understanding of negotiation skills and dynamics in the context of United Nations conferences and the UNFCCC process. The programme supported the capacities of the Government of the Republic of Kenya to prepare effectively for COP26 of the UNFCCC.
